note: Web research against Polish Wikipedia + zabytek.pl + parish/heritage sources. All ten confirmed. Ambiguity notes below are load-bearing — read before authoring cards.
ambiguities: ⭐ CROSS-REFERENCE: 'Kościół św. Józefa' and 'Kościół Wniebowzięcia NMP' are the SAME FOUNDATION. The wooden church was the original Assumption parish church on Plac Kościelny; when the brick Assumption church replaced it (1887–97), the wooden one was moved to Ogrodowa and rededicated to St. Joseph. The place cards should reference each other.
Kościół Świętej Anny — the archdiocese also has a St. Anne parish at Wrzeszczewice, outside the city. Researched entry is the Łódź-Zarzew one at al. Śmigłego-Rydza, near Księży Młyn.

Archikatedra architect attribution is genuinely contested: Polish Wikipedia leads with Wende + Zarske and places Zillmann as involved; other sources foreground Zillmann. All listed. Dates and height are solid.
Kościół Zesłania Ducha Świętego rebuild end date appears as both 1891 and 1892; 1889–1892 used, per the Wikipedia article body.
Heinzel chapel is in the CATHOLIC section of the Old Cemetery; Scheibler chapel in the EVANGELICAL-AUGSBURG section — same Ogrodowa necropolis, different confessional halves.

entries.name: Kościół pw. Świętego Józefa Oblubieńca Najświętszej Maryi Panny
entries.architect: Fryderyk Hoffman (1835–37 enlargement); Konstanty Wojciechowski (1888 relocation)
entries.blurb: Larch-log church of 1765–68, funded by Bishop Antoni Ostrowski. Moved whole from Plac Kościelny to Ogrodowa in 1888, reportedly in a single day.
entries.why_notable: The oldest church in Łódź and the only surviving building from the town's pre-industrial farming era.

entries.name: Kaplica Rodziny Heinzlów
entries.blurb: Domed mausoleum, 10.4 × 9.5 m, modelled on Wawel's Sigismund Chapel. Commissioned by Paulina Heinzel for her husband, textile magnate Juliusz Heinzel.
entries.why_notable: One of the last monumental family burial chapels built in this style on Polish soil.

entries.name: Kościół Wniebowzięcia Najświętszej Maryi Panny
entries.blurb: Red unplastered brick, 55 × 42 m, two towers, three naves. Replaced the wooden church now standing on Ogrodowa; over half the cost came from Łódź industrialists.
entries.why_notable: Seat of the oldest Catholic parish in Łódź — for roughly five centuries the town's only one.

entries.name: Kościół Zesłania Ducha Świętego
entries.architect: Bonifacy Witkowski (1826); Otto Gehlig and Hilary Majewski (rebuild)
entries.style: Eclectic, predominantly neo-Renaissance with Romanesque windows
entries.blurb: Built as the Lutheran Holy Trinity church at Piotrkowska 2, on a Greek-cross plan roughly 30 × 29 m with four corner towers and a central dome. Catholic since 1945.
entries.why_notable: The Evangelical mother church of industrial Łódź, anchoring Plac Wolności at the head of Piotrkowska.

entries.name: Archikatedra pw. Świętego Stanisława Kostki
entries.architect: Johannes Wende and Adolf Zarske, with Emil Zillmann; later work by Józef Pius Dziekoński, Sławomir Odrzywolski-Nałęcz and Stefan Szyller
entries.blurb: Pale-yellow unplastered brick basilica, 104.5 m to the spire, loosely modelled on Ulm Minster. Funded by an 1895 committee of manufacturers including Heinzel, Herbst and Kunitzer.
entries.why_notable: Tallest building in Łódź; cathedral since 1920, minor basilica since 1989.

entries.name: Cerkiew Zaśnięcia Najświętszej Maryi Panny
entries.blurb: Brick cemetery church of 1904 in the Orthodox section of the Doły necropolis, Telefoniczna 4. Serves the St. Alexander Nevsky parish; heritage-listed 1983.
entries.why_notable: The Orthodox cemetery church of Łódź, and Chełmiński's larger companion to his St. Olga chapel.

entries.name: Cerkiew św. Olgi
entries.blurb: Single-nave brick church at Piramowicza 12, built with an Orthodox orphanage on land given by Juliusz Kunitzer in 1891. Its iconostasis was rejected as too tall for the Nevsky cathedral.
entries.why_notable: The only Orthodox church dedicated to St. Olga in Poland.

entries.name: Kaplica Rodziny Scheibler
entries.architect: Edward Lilpop and Józef Pius Dziekoński
entries.blurb: 37 m mausoleum on a Latin-cross plan, sandstone-clad brick, with eight zinc angels by Andrzej Pruszyński. Commissioned by Anna Scheibler after two failed design competitions.
entries.why_notable: Among the largest works of cemetery architecture anywhere; listed in 2006 among the world's 100 most endangered monuments.

entries.name: Sobór św. Aleksandra Newskiego
entries.blurb: Orthodox cathedral at Kilińskiego 56, paid for by Łódź factory owners — Scheibler 25,000 roubles, Heinzel 11,000, Poznański 8,000 — as a display of loyalty to the tsar.
entries.why_notable: Cathedral of the Łódź-Poznań diocese; built to mark Alexander II's survival of the 1879 Solovyov assassination attempt.

entries.name: Kościół Świętej Anny
entries.blurb: Single-nave pressed-brick church of about 640 m² at al. Śmigłego-Rydza 24/26, in the former village of Zarzew. Consecrated 10 December 1905; parish erected 1909.
entries.why_notable: Marks the absorption of the farming village of Zarzew into industrial Łódź.
